newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's health normal, surgeon tells Tass.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's health normal, surgeon tells Tass.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's health is stable and as it should be, the surgeon who led the Russian president's heart bypass operation said on Saturday.
"The state of Boris Yeltsin's health is normal, everything is stable. There is no need to wish for better," Itar-Tass news agency quoted heart surgeon Renat Akchurin as saying.
Akchurin, who led the quintuple bypass on November 5, said Yeltsin had already been speaking of returning to work in the Kremlin for a long time.
Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin's chief doctor, Sergei Mironov, on Friday as saying Yeltsin could return to the Kremlin for brief visits as early as next week.
Mironov said doctors would decide next week whether Yeltsin, who is being treated in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, could move to his official residence in the same compound.
Yeltsin, dogged by ill health, has spent very little time in the Kremlin since he was re-elected for a second term on July 3.
Akchurin was speaking before a Moscow concert to which Yeltsin's medical team, members of the president's family and other doctors were invited.
